caption:
Two rich countries, almost the same median income — and two completely different shapes.

Watch the American curve run from $24 a day at the 10th percentile to $169 at the 90th, while Denmark runs from $32 to $97. Half the spread, forty years running.

📊 See how the United States and Denmark distribute their income from 1980 to 2024 in this animated distribution: share of population by daily income in 2017 PPP dollars, across 105 logarithmic brackets. Explore what inequality looks like when you draw it as a shape rather than a number.

Source: Gapminder Income Mountains (v3), from World Bank PovcalNet / PIP, via open-numbers (CC BY 4.0). Bracket 20 starts at $2.00 a day; each bracket is 1.32 times the previous one. Modelled estimates.
